children: , the social-media and digital-advertising giant, entered a tougher regulatory era in California on Friday. Investors brushed off the immediate threat, sending the stock approximately 1.3% higher to $652.47 in late-morning trading.

Gov. Gavin Newsom signed 13 bills targeting social media and artificial intelligence, according to Reuters. The rules restrict platforms from showing users under 16 potentially addictive features such as infinite scrolling and algorithmic autoplay, while chatbot providers face tighter parental-control and safety-review obligations. The Associated Press said negligent large platforms could face penalties of up to $1 million for each child harmed.

That maximum individual fine equals roughly 0.0016% of Meta's latest quarterly revenue of $60.8 billion, but thousands of claims could change the math quickly. The picture also shows Meta trading 23.32% below its GF Value estimate of $850.92, suggesting the market already applies a meaningful discount to the shares. The real danger is not one fineit is a forced redesign of the recommendation engine that drives engagement, advertising inventory and personalization.

title: Meta Gains Despite California's Million-Dollar Youth-AI Threat
